content.value_statement: Meeting transcripts can hide repeated communication habits that are hard to see in the moment. This skill turns those transcripts into focused coaching insights with examples and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews local meeting transcripts in text, Markdown, VTT, SRT, or document formats.
Identifies patterns such as conflict avoidance, filler words, interruptions, and directness.
Estimates speaking ratios, question patterns, and turn-taking behavior from transcripts.
Provides timestamped examples when source transcripts include timestamps.
Compares communication patterns across multiple meetings or time periods.
Produces actionable recommendations for leadership, facilitation, and listening skills.
limitations: Analysis quality depends on transcript accuracy, speaker labels, and available timestamps.
It does not verify tone, intent, or body language beyond what appears in transcripts.
It cannot analyze recordings directly unless transcripts are already available.
It should not replace professional coaching, HR guidance, or legal review.

use_cases.title: Improve Personal Communication
use_cases.description: Find repeated habits such as hedging, interruptions, filler words, or unclear requests across recent meetings.

use_cases.title: Prepare Leadership Reviews
use_cases.description: Collect concrete transcript examples that show facilitation strengths, growth areas, and progress over time.

use_cases.title: Coach Team Conversations
use_cases.description: Review meeting dynamics, speaking balance, inclusion patterns, and follow-up clarity for team development.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a single behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these meeting transcripts for one pattern: when I use hedging language instead of direct requests. Include examples and practical alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Review Facilitation Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my team meeting transcripts and summarize my facilitation style. Focus on speaking balance, questions, disagreement handling, and inclusion of quieter participants.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Periods
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my meetings from Q1 and Q2. Show whether interruptions, clarifying questions, filler words, and active listening improved or declined.

prompt_templates.title: Build Development Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all transcripts in this folder, rank my top three communication growth areas, cite the strongest examples, and create a four-week improvement plan.

output_examples.input: A manager asks for conflict avoidance patterns across recent one-on-one meetings.
output: Summary of repeated indirect language and missed moments for direct feedback.
Two or three transcript examples with meeting names and timestamps when available.
Alternative phrasing for each example and a short practice goal for the next meeting.

output_examples.input: A team lead asks how their facilitation style changed between two quarters.
output: Comparison of speaking ratio, question frequency, interruptions, and inclusion signals.
Plain-language assessment of improved listening and remaining facilitation risks.
Recommended next steps for meeting structure, agenda control, and follow-up clarity.

output_examples.input: A professional asks for filler word and clarity feedback from customer calls.
output: List of common filler words and the contexts where they appear most often.
Examples of unclear statements with clearer alternatives.
A concise action plan for practicing direct, confident language.

best_practices: Use transcripts with clear speaker labels, dates, and meeting names for better attribution.
Ask for one or two behaviors at a time when you need detailed coaching feedback.
Review sensitive transcripts locally and remove information that is not needed for the analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not use transcript analysis to make employment decisions without human review and policy guidance.
Do not ask for conclusions about intent, emotion, or competence that transcripts cannot support.
Do not mix unrelated meetings or missing speaker labels when comparing communication trends.

faq.question: What transcript formats can this skill review?
faq.answer: It is designed for text-based transcripts such as TXT, Markdown, VTT, SRT, and exported document text.

faq.question: Can it analyze audio or video recordings directly?
faq.answer: No. It needs transcripts or meeting notes that already contain the spoken content.

faq.question: Does it work with multiple meetings at once?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare patterns across folders, date ranges, or groups of transcript files.

faq.question: Can it identify who speaks the most?
faq.answer: Yes, when transcripts include reliable speaker labels and enough structure to estimate speaking turns.

faq.question: How should sensitive meeting data be handled?
faq.answer: Keep transcripts local when possible, remove unrelated confidential details, and follow your organization's data rules.

faq.question: Is the feedback a substitute for professional coaching?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured observations from transcripts, but human judgment is needed for coaching and personnel decisions.
